lesson_title: The Big Belly That Means Hunger: Reading Food and Its Absence
hook_text: A child with a big round belly can be dangerously underfed. Here is why.
clip_script: Your body is a house being built while you live in it. It needs fuel, bricks and spare parts. Fuel is carbohydrates and fats: pap, bread, oil, nuts. A gram of fat holds more than twice the energy of a gram of starch, which is why fried snacks pack so many kilojoules. Bricks are proteins: beans, eggs, pilchards, amasi, even mopane worms, rebuilt into your muscle, your blood and your enzymes. Spare parts are vitamins and minerals: vitamin A for your eyes, C for your gums, D and calcium for your bones, iron for your blood, iodine for your neck. Now the twist. A small child fed almost only starch, with too little protein, can develop kwashiorkor. Fluid leaks into the tissues and the belly swells up round, while the arms stay thin and the hair turns pale. That belly is not a full child. It is a hungry one. The fix is on the plate: half vegetables and fruit, a quarter starch, a quarter protein.
visual_style: A house under construction with labelled fuel cans, bricks and a spare-parts box; food icons drop into each; a gentle illustrated child silhouette with a swollen belly and thin arms, then a balanced plate divided into halves and quarters.
mood: Caring, clear, serious at the turn.
pacing: Quick house metaphor, a steady nutrient list, a slow, serious beat on kwashiorkor, a hopeful plate finish.
